newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal Prime Minister Deuba says he will resign.
newsitem.headline: Nepal Prime Minister Deuba says he will resign.

text.p: Nepal's Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba said on Thursday he would resign after his 17-month-old centre-right coalition lost a crucial parliamentary vote of confidence.

"I accept the verdict gracefully and I will resign," Deuba told Reuters after the vote. Asked when he will resign, he said: "I will have to check whether to personally go to the King (Birendra) or if I can send my resignation," he said.

Deuba's government received 101 votes against a required minimum of 103 during voting on the motion which he had moved to demonstrate the coalition's majority in the 205-seat lower house of parliament. Ninety-two MP's voted against the motion.
Birodh Khatiwada, a deputy of the opposition United Marxist Leninist (UML) party told Reuters: "We will have to make moves to form an alternative now."
Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party, which has 87 seats, lost its majority last December following a split in the ranks of a partner, the Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), which had 19 seats.
Deuba's coalition had replaced a minority government formed by the communist UML, which lost power in 1995. The next parliamentary elections are officially not due until 1999.
